title: US and Hungary sign agreements on law enforcement and energy infrastructure
excerpt: Secretary Rubio and Foreign Minister Orbán signed two memorandums of understanding regarding law enforcement cooperation and regional energy infrastructure.
bodyHtml:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orbán signed two memorandums of understanding in Washington, DC, on October 29, 2026. The ceremony was held in the Colin L. Powell Treaty Room.

The first memorandum concerns law enforcement cooperation and information exchange. Secretary Rubio stated that the agreement aims to confront what he described as a resurgence of far-left terrorism. Foreign Minister Orbán noted that the agreement will enhance information sharing to prevent, detect, and prosecute violence by left-wing groups, specifically citing Antifa Ost. Secretary Rubio stated that these movements operate off the basis of an international network that seeks to destabilize Western societies.

The second memorandum concerns energy infrastructure and regional energy security. This agreement is signed within the framework of the Trump Peace Pipelines initiative. The initiative is intended to meet Central Europe’s energy needs through the export of United States energy. Foreign Minister Orbán stated the agreement will enhance the energy infrastructure of central Eastern Europe in both oil and gas.
